calas:Banje.name: Banje
calas:Banje.teaser: The city's own pebble beach, two minutes outside Ploče Gate, with the walls rising behind your towel
calas:Banje.story: Banje is where Dubrovnik goes for a swim without leaving town. Walk out through Ploče Gate, past the old Lazareti quarantine buildings, and the road drops to a curve of fine pebbles facing Lokrum, with the Old Port and the eastern walls framing the view back. The front of the beach is a beach club with rows of paid loungers; the rest is public and free, and that is where the locals spread out on their own towels. In late October the sea here is usually around 20 °C, cool but swimmable on a still, sunny day, and the summer setup of loungers, parasols and the club's service winds down for the winter.
calas:Banje.why: The quickest swim from the Old Town, and the best low-level view of the walls from the water.
facts: On foot, about two minutes east of Ploče Gate along the road towards the Excelsior; steps lead down from the street
Early morning, before the loungers fill, or late afternoon when the walls catch the low sun

Your own towel for the free section and water shoes for the pebbles; loungers and parasols are a paid, seasonal extra (about EUR 33 for a pair of loungers and a parasol in season, Oct 2026, secondary source)
Swim a few strokes out and turn round: the Old Port and the Revelin side of the walls line up behind the beach

calas:The rocks under the south wall.name: The rocks under the south wall
calas:The rocks under the south wall.teaser: Flat limestone shelves below the sea wall, a ladder, and ten metres of clear water straight down
calas:The rocks under the south wall.story: There is no beach on the seaward side of the Old Town, only the rock the walls stand on. Go past the cathedral and through one of the small openings in the south wall by the Buža bars and you come out on flat shelves of pale limestone just above the water. Steel ladders lead down into the sea, which is deep and clear straight off the rock, and on summer afternoons the sound is of bodies hitting water as people jump from the higher ledges. There is no sand, no shade and no lifeguard. By late October the water is around 20 °C and the crowd has gone, but the swell can pick up quickly when the wind turns south.
calas:The rocks under the south wall.why: Swimming in open water with the city wall over your head is something only this town offers.
facts: Inside the Old Town: from the cathedral side, follow the lanes up to the south wall and go through the openings by the Buža bars (their own card is under Boire)
Mid-morning on a calm day, while the rock is in sun and before the bars fill
Water shoes, a towel to lie on, a mask; nothing to rent here
Look up from the water at the curve of the wall and the shuttered windows above it

calas:Sveti Jakov.name: Sveti Jakov
calas:Sveti Jakov.teaser: A pebble cove at the bottom of some 160 steps, with the whole walled city laid out to the west
calas:Sveti Jakov.story: Sveti Jakov takes its name from the small church of St James on the cliff above it, a short way east of Ploče along Vlaha Bukovca. The only way down is a long stone staircase, around 150 to 160 steps depending on who is counting, and that staircase is what keeps the cove quieter than Banje. At the bottom is a curve of pebbles and clear water, a small bar and restaurant, and, looking west past Lokrum, the walls of the Old Town seen end-on from the sea. Kayaks set off from here for Lokrum in summer. In late October the sea is around 20 °C and the bar and loungers may already be packed away: check before you count on lunch.
calas:Sveti Jakov.why: The view back to the walls from the water is the best of any beach near town.
facts: Bus 8 to the last stop or a taxi to the church of Sveti Jakov on Vlaha Bukovca, then down the staircase; parking near the church is limited and paid
Late afternoon, when the light falls on the walls to the west
Water, water shoes for the pebbles, and legs for the climb back up; not suitable for anyone who struggles with steps
Swim out until Lokrum and the Old Town line up together

calas:Lokrum.name: Lokrum
calas:Lokrum.teaser: A wooded reserve ten minutes off the Old Port, with peacocks, a salt lake and a rule: everyone leaves by night
calas:Lokrum.story: Lokrum sits about 600 m off the Old Port and nobody lives on it: overnight stays are banned, and the last boat takes everyone back to town in the evening. Benedictines founded an abbey here in 1023; Archduke Maximilian of Habsburg bought the island in the 1850s, built a summer house on the monastery ruins, laid out gardens and brought peacocks, whose descendants still strut the paths and scream from the pines. The island has been a protected reserve since 1964. Walk from the harbour to the cloister, where a replica Iron Throne recalls the Game of Thrones filming, then on to the Mrtvo More, the 'Dead Sea', a small salt lake fed by the sea through the rock, warm, sheltered and shallow enough for children. The southern shore is bare rock dropping into deep water.
calas:Lokrum.why: The quietest swim within sight of the walls, and a pine-shaded walk when the Old Town is full.
facts: Reserve boat from the Old Port, about 10-15 minutes; in the 2026 summer timetable the first boat left at 09:00 and the last return from Lokrum was at 20:00. Adult return with reserve entry EUR 27-30 (sources differ, Oct 2026). Boats are weather-dependent and the island has closed for the winter in past years (it reopened on 1 February 2025): check lokrum.hr for the 2026 closing date
The first boat, before the day-trippers; the peacocks are most active in the cool of the morning
A picnic, water and water shoes; dogs, fires and smoking are banned on the island
A swim in the Mrtvo More, then the botanical garden around Maximilian's house

sources.label: Croatia Week, the island no one would stay on overnight

calas:Lopud and Šunj.name: Lopud and Šunj
calas:Lopud and Šunj.teaser: The ferry to Lopud, then a walk across the island through pines to the rare thing on this coast: sand
calas:Lopud and Šunj.story: Lopud is the middle of the three inhabited Elaphiti islands, the name from the Greek for deer, and the one with the beach. Step off the ferry onto the village waterfront and take the lane inland near the ruins of the old Grand Hotel; a signed path climbs through shady pine woods and drops to Šunj on the far side. It is a sandy bay protected by a breakwater, shallow for about 100 m, which on a coast of pebbles and rock is the reason people make the trip. Visitors leave cars behind: in summer golf carts shuttle between port and beach. In late October the sea is around 20 °C, the beach bars and rentals are winding down and the island goes quiet.
calas:Lopud and Šunj.why: The one proper sand beach within a ferry ride of Dubrovnik, with a forest walk to earn it.
facts: Jadrolinija line 807 from Gruž (Dubrovnik - Koločep - Lopud - Suđurađ on Šipan); its off-season timetable runs 28 September to 31 December 2026, with fewer sailings on Sundays and holidays (Oct 2026). From Lopud harbour, walk 20-45 minutes across the island
Take a morning boat and plan the return around the last ferry back; sailings can be cancelled in bad weather
Water, shoes for the path, and food in the off-season, when the beach bars may be shut
The walk itself: the path passes chapels and the ruins of a fort on the way to the bay

avoid:The cruise-day crush.name: The cruise-day crush
avoid:The cruise-day crush.teaser: On a big ship day, thousands of day visitors pour through Pile Gate within a few hours
avoid:The cruise-day crush.story: Dubrovnik's cruise berths are at Gruž, a few kilometres from the walls, and when the big ships are in, buses and shuttles deliver their passengers to Pile Gate in a single wave. Stradun, a street about 300 m long, then carries thousands of day visitors at once and the walls queue at the stairs. The city has pushed back: the Port Authority limits berthing to two large ships a day and has capped cruise visitors in town at about 4,000 at a time, yet some 461 cruise calls were scheduled for 2026. The ships keep to a timetable, so the crush can be planned around.
avoid:The cruise-day crush.why: Check the ship calendar before going ashore and you can have the Old Town nearly to yourself.
facts: Tour groups behind numbered paddles filling Stradun and Pile Gate from mid-morning; the season is winding down in late October but ships still call
Check the Dubrovnik Port Authority's ship schedule; walk the Old Town before 09:00 or after 18:30, and on heavy days go to Lokrum, Lapad or Cavtat instead

sources.label: Maritime Executive, Dubrovnik puts cap on daily cruise ship arrivals

avoid:Prijeko Street.name: Prijeko Street
avoid:Prijeko Street.teaser: The long lane parallel to Stradun where the menus come in eight languages and a waiter blocks your way
avoid:Prijeko Street.story: Prijeko runs the length of the Old Town one block north of Stradun, a straight lane of terraces under the stairs that climb to the walls. It has become the town's tourist-menu row: laminated cards in eight to ten languages, photos of every dish, hosts stepping into your path, and 'fresh fish' that has often come from a freezer. The exception is Stara Loža, the one Prijeko address this guide keeps (its own card is under the tables). The honest konobas are a stair or two away, in the side lanes that cross between Stradun and the walls.
avoid:Prijeko Street.why: Two minutes' walk to a side lane gets a better plate for the same money.
facts: Picture menus, touts at every terrace and fish displays with no species or boat named
Eat in Antuninska, Boškovićeva or Palmotićeva, or ask the waiter what came off the boat today and where

avoid:Pizza by the slice on Stradun.name: Pizza on Stradun
avoid:Pizza by the slice on Stradun.teaser: Frozen bases and microwaved slices at main-street prices, a short walk from a real pizza oven
avoid:Pizza by the slice on Stradun.story: The cafés in the middle of Stradun sell pizza to people who are hungry and in a hurry, and many of them sell it that way: a frozen base, reheated, at a price set by the address. Sit-down pizza inside the walls runs around EUR 15-20 according to 2026 price guides, and the slice counters charge for the view, not the dough. Outside Ploče Gate, Pizzeria Tabasco fires its pizzas properly (its own card is under the tables), and a quick snack in the Old Town is better spent at Buffet Škola.
avoid:Pizza by the slice on Stradun.why: Walk five minutes beyond the gate and the same money buys a pizza made to order.
facts: Pre-baked slices under glass and cafés on Stradun with a pizza board by the door
Pizzeria Tabasco up Hvarska outside Ploče, or a pršut sandwich at Buffet Škola

avoid:Oysters inside the walls.name: Oysters inside the walls
avoid:Oysters inside the walls.teaser: The oysters on Old Town menus come from Mali Ston, an hour up the coast: eat them there instead
avoid:Oysters inside the walls.story: Dubrovnik's oysters are not from Dubrovnik. They are farmed in the bay at Mali Ston, about an hour north-west by road, and reach the Old Town by van. An oyster keeps, but it does not improve: a plate inside the walls may have spent days in transit and cold storage, especially in the shoulder season when restaurants buy less often, and it is served at Old Town prices. At Mali Ston the same shellfish comes off the rafts in the bay you are looking at. The oyster itself, its protected name and its season, have their own card under the table.
avoid:Oysters inside the walls.why: A plate on the Mali Ston quay beats any 'fresh' claim on a Stradun menu.
facts: 'Fresh Ston oysters' chalked on boards in the Old Town, with no date of harvest
Drive to Mali Ston and eat them on the quay at Bota Šare or Vila Koruna; in the city, ask when they arrived before you order

avoid:Truffle on the menu.name: Truffle on the menu
avoid:Truffle on the menu.teaser: Croatia's truffle country is Istria, far to the north: here it is usually imported, or oil
avoid:Truffle on the menu.story: Truffle is the flavour of Istria, at the other end of the Croatian coast, where the oak woods of the Mirna valley are hunted with dogs. It is not part of the Dubrovnik kitchen, and when it turns up on an Old Town menu, shaved over pasta or in a 'truffle risotto', it has either travelled a long way or come out of a bottle of truffle-flavoured oil. A menu that leads with truffle is telling you it was written for visitors. The local plate is elsewhere: šporki makaruli, black risotto, brodet, the lamb from under the peka.
avoid:Truffle on the menu.why: When truffle is the headline, read it as a sign to keep walking.
facts: Truffle pasta, truffle fries and truffle risotto on Old Town boards, with no producer named
Order what the city cooks itself, crni rižot or brodet; save truffle for a trip to Istria

follow:Dubrovnik Tourist Board.name: Dubrovnik Tourist Board
follow:Dubrovnik Tourist Board.teaser: The city's own tourist board: events, opening seasons and the practical pages that stay current
follow:Dubrovnik Tourist Board.story: The Turistička zajednica grada Dubrovnika runs the city's official visitor site and information offices. It is the place to check what is actually on: the events calendar from the Feast of St Blaise in February to the Winter Festival in December, museum and sight pages, the Lokrum and nature-reserve pages, and practical notes on transport and parking. In late October it is also where the end of the season shows first, as summer programmes come down and the winter festival is announced.
follow:Dubrovnik Tourist Board.why: One official site for what is open this week, without the reseller noise.
facts: The official tourist board of the City of Dubrovnik
Croatian and English, with other languages on parts of the site
The events calendar, the sights pages and the practical information section

follow:Dubrovnik Summer Festival.name: Dubrovnik Summer Festival
follow:Dubrovnik Summer Festival.teaser: The festival that turns forts, squares and stairs into stages for six weeks every summer
follow:Dubrovnik Summer Festival.story: The Dubrovnik Summer Festival has used the city itself as its theatre since 1950: plays on the fortress of Lovrijenac, concerts in the Rector's Palace atrium, opera and dance on the squares. The 2026 edition, the 77th, ran from 10 July to 25 August with more than 2,000 performers. Its official site publishes the programme in spring, opens ticket sales and lists the venues, which matters because the festival's evenings close streets and fill the Old Town. The calendar card in this guide tells the festival itself.
follow:Dubrovnik Summer Festival.why: Follow it from spring to book the open-air nights before they sell out.
facts: The official site of the Dubrovnik Summer Festival; usually 10 July to 25 August. The 2027 dates were not yet announced by the festival in October 2026
The programme, the venue list and the ticket pages

sources.label: Croatia Week, 77th Dubrovnik Summer Festival opens

follow:The Dubrovnik Times.name: The Dubrovnik Times
follow:The Dubrovnik Times.teaser: The town's English-language paper: road closures, ship days, openings and what the locals argue about
follow:The Dubrovnik Times.story: The Dubrovnik Times is the city's English-language news outlet, edited by Mark Thomas, a British journalist who has lived in Dubrovnik for decades. It began as a printed weekly, an idea encouraged by the editor of the local Croatian paper, Dubrovački vjesnik, on the reasoning that visitors wanted local news they could read. Today it runs mostly online: city council decisions, cruise and traffic stories, restaurant openings, weather warnings and the town's long debate about how many visitors it can take.
follow:The Dubrovnik Times.why: The fastest way, in English, to learn what is closed, delayed or new this week.
facts: Dubrovnik's English-language local news site and paper, edited by Mark Thomas
Local news, events and the traffic and weather notices

sources.label: Visit Croatia, interview with Mark Thomas of the Dubrovnik Times

follow:Jadrolinija.name: Jadrolinija
follow:Jadrolinija.teaser: Croatia's state ferry line, and the only timetable that counts for the islands in winter
follow:Jadrolinija.story: Jadrolinija, the state shipping line based in Rijeka, runs the public ferries and catamarans out of Gruž: line 807 to Koločep, Lopud and Šipan, plus the routes to Mljet and Korčula. Its timetables split the year into seasons, and from late September the island boats drop to an off-season pattern with fewer sailings, fewer still on Sundays and holidays. Weather cancels boats too. Download the line's timetable PDF for the date you travel rather than trusting a summer table copied onto a blog.
follow:Jadrolinija.why: Out of season, check it the night before every island day.
facts: Croatia's state ferry and catamaran operator; line 807 serves the Elaphiti from Gruž, with an off-season timetable from 28 September to 31 December 2026
The route pages, the timetable PDFs for each season and the service notices

follow:Dubrovnik Port Authority.name: Dubrovnik Port Authority
follow:Dubrovnik Port Authority.teaser: The port's own list of which cruise ships are due in Gruž, and on which day
follow:Dubrovnik Port Authority.story: The Lučka uprava Dubrovnik, the Dubrovnik Port Authority, runs the cruise berths at Gruž and the Old Port anchorage and decides which ships may come in on which day under its berthing policy, published two years ahead. For anyone planning a day in the Old Town, its arrivals list is the most useful page in the city: two or more big ships means a crowded Stradun from mid-morning, an empty berth means a quiet day. In 2026 some 461 cruise calls were scheduled.
follow:Dubrovnik Port Authority.why: Read the ship list before you pick the day for the walls.
facts: The authority that runs Dubrovnik's cruise port and publishes the ship arrival schedule; guides give its site as portdubrovnik.hr
The cruise ship arrivals schedule and the berthing policy
